sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 12:28

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 12:28:1
items.html:
His phases of Hod, Yesod, and Malchut, which are mixed there in those seven kings, were not all sorted: You already know that ZA includes the five Hassadim and the five Gevurot, that his own phase is the five Hassadim, and the phase of the Malchut within him is the five Gevurot. Now here, in the Ibur of ZA, only his own phase — that is, the five Hassadim — was sorted completely; but the five Gevurot, which are the phase of the Malchut within him, were not sorted completely. And the reason is that his Malchut must become a separate Partzuf of her own, called the Nukva of ZA, which is not corrected except after the greatness of ZA, as the ARI wrote above (page 772, item 60). And therefore these five Gevurot that are now corrected in ZA are only the phase of the Nukva that is in his body; so there is not yet a complete sorting of his Malchut now, but only one part of it, needed for the phase of the Nukva that is in his body. And therefore it is reckoned that the five Gevurot of ZA were not all corrected, but only some of them. As is clarified.
And not only that, but even the five Hassadim were not all sorted, for it is known that the five Hassadim are HGT NH, wherein KHB descended to the phase of HGT, and Netzah is ZA, and Hod is the Nukva. And it is found, for the reason above, that the Hod of the five Hassadim too could not be sorted completely — that is, those parts belonging to the separate Nukva of ZA, because the Hod of the five Hassadim is the phase of Malchut, as is clarified. And since Hod was not sorted completely, so too, as stated, Yesod and Malchut could not be sorted completely, for you know that the two vessels Yesod and Malchut are the expansion of the vessel of Hod. (As above, page 336, the passage beginning “And now.”) And it is thus found that these three vessels — Hod, Yesod, and Malchut — could not all be sorted now, at the time of the Ibur. And this was so both in general and in particular, that is, in the general Hod, Yesod, and Malchut, and also in the Hod, Yesod, and Malchut that are in every single vessel from Keter to Malchut, as the ARI writes here. And see what is written further on this matter below, in the adjacent item.
